From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## The "[STANDARD]" labels and the Reviewer Efficiency Note

The Seller's package ends with a note saying that items marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." Nothing in our baseline supports this. These are the Seller's opening positions in a Seller draft.

I have reviewed every item on its merits, and I recommend you tell Seller's counsel in writing that **no clause is agreed until marked up and accepted by the Buyer**. Most of the substantive risk sits in the clauses labelled [STANDARD].

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 40–50% (AUD 9.6m–12m), given the open Bluefen, privacy, Ironquay and debt items. Title, capacity and tax should sit outside this cap at 100% of price. Specific indemnities should be uncapped or capped at price.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50%, landing no lower than 30–35%. **Reason:** A 20% cap is light for a target with roughly 30% customer concentration and an unresolved data incident.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis, plus a AUD 250,000 deductible basket where only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A de minimis of about AUD 10,000–15,000. Related claims should aggregate toward it. The basket should be about AUD 120,000 (0.5%) and **tipping**, so the Buyer recovers from the first dollar once it is crossed. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure and accept a tipping basket. **Reason:** A deductible basket at about 1% of price means the Buyer permanently absorbs the first AUD 250k of proven loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. The Seller also wants "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties, so that at least two audit cycles fall within the period. Tax claims should run 5–7 years, or until 60 days after the ATO/OSR amendment period expires. Title and capacity claims should run 6–7 years. Specific indemnities should have their own periods.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default. **Reason:** That default quietly imports an 18-month bar onto tax, title and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties carry the same 20% cap and 18-month limit, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, with a 6–7 year limit and no de minimis or basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, so a AUD 4.8m cap is not an administrative matter.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Under cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out from every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause. It should cover fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company and their officers and advisers. The non-reliance clause should not purport to cover statements in the Warranties or the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Make this non-negotiable. **Reason:** As drafted, the Seller could cap its liability for its own fraud. The non-reliance clause could also be used to defeat causation in an ACL s18 misleading conduct claim.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter para 1.1–1.2 generally discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter. Each disclosure should carry enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely financial effect, and should reference the specific warranty it qualifies. There should be no general disclosure of the data room. At most, the Buyer could accept specified public searches made on a stated date.
- **Recommendation:** Delete para 1.1 and narrow para 1.2. Para 1.4 (non-admission) can stay. **Reason:** General disclosure converts every buried data room document into a warranty exclusion.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Under cl 8.3, there is no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, *or* that was discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** An express clause that Buyer knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, does not reduce or prevent any claim. The only exception should be matters fairly disclosed under SPA-N-006.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Fall back, at most, to the *actual* knowledge of named individuals of the specific breach. **Reason:** A "discoverable" knowledge test combined with general disclosure would nullify the warranties almost entirely.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Under cl 3 and 6.3, the Seller uses reasonable endeavours, and the condition is satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure para 2 confirms that no consent exists yet and that the cl 11.3 conditions are not shown as satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** A Condition Precedent requiring:
  - unconditional written consent from Bluefen, or consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably;
  - satisfaction or waiver of the cl 11.3 conditions;
  - no notice of termination or of an adverse change in terms.

  The Seller should be under a "best" or "all reasonable" endeavours obligation. Only the Buyer should be able to waive the condition. There should be a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right, and a warranty that the consent remains in force at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft as a firm CP. **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or 30%, of FY26 revenue. A conditional consent could still leave the contract terminable.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release of the facility (about AUD 3.2m) to follow *after* Completion. Disclosure para 3 confirms it is unpaid and no discharge has been given.
- **Buyer should want:** The following delivered *at* Completion:
  - a payout letter;
  - a deed of release;
  - a PPSR financing statement discharge and release of all security;
  - payment of the facility from the purchase price as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

  The Buyer should also receive a waiver of the cl 8.1 change of control default, if needed, or a pre-Completion payout.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. **Reason:** Without a release at Completion, the Buyer acquires a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt that may be in default on change of control.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 in DD-005 bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not shown in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses and all associated amounts (PAYG withholding, superannuation if applicable, NSW payroll tax, and any workers' compensation or leave on-costs) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt. They should be deducted from the price or paid through Completion payroll, and backed by a specific indemnity.
  - Indicative on-costs are up to about AUD 75k (super at roughly 12% and NSW payroll tax at roughly 5.45%), subject to tax advice on whether the bonuses count as ordinary time earnings.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow as a price deduction. **Reason:** The Company is the employer, so these become Company liabilities post-Completion unless the funds flow says otherwise.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment of AUD 180k. Disclosure para 4 confirms there is no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment, and that title to the SOW3 materials depends on payment (DD-004 cl 7.3).
- **Buyer should want:** A CP requiring evidence of cleared payment (or payment at Completion from the Seller's proceeds) and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. The Buyer should also get a specific indemnity covering *all* loss from any failure to own the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims, re-development costs and business interruption. That indemnity should sit outside the cap, the thresholds and the general time limit. A retention should apply if the CP is waived.
- **Recommendation:** Expand the indemnity and add the CP. **Reason:** The risk is losing core IP, not a AUD 180k invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Called "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Disclosure para 6 confirms that about 1,240 records may have been exposed and that access, scope and notification are all unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Before Completion: a completed forensic investigation, a documented assessment under Privacy Act Part IIIC (the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme), and an OAIC and individual notification decision.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, thresholds and time limit, covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party or class claims.
  - A retention or escrow of, for example, AUD 500k–1m pending resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller's characterisation. Raise this as urgent. **Reason:** The incident was known by 22 September, so the 30-day assessment window has probably passed. A late or missed notification is itself a compliance exposure.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are said to be ordinary-course costs. Disclosure para 8 asks that they be "read together" and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of DD-008 and DD-011 and an explanation of the timing. The renewals look as if they may have been split to stay under an approval threshold, and the Buyer should check for any related-party connection.
  - The renewals should be brought within the conduct-of-business covenants so that Buyer consent is required.
  - Any prepaid or committed amount not in the ordinary course should be treated as Debt, or covered by a specific indemnity.
  - The Buyer should get warranties that the renewals are on arm's-length terms and terminable.
- **Recommendation:** Hold as an open diligence item and add a price-adjustment hook. **Reason:** Three identical related renewals flagged to be read together is a red flag, not evidence of ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** The proposal that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" collapses all claim types into one regime. The [STANDARD] labelling also presents the package as agreed.
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct, expressly drafted regimes, each with its own cap, thresholds and time limit:
  1. General warranties
  2. Fundamental (title and capacity)
  3. Tax warranties and indemnity
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Sandbar)
  5. Fraud, which should be unlimited

  Price adjustments and Debt items should be dealt with in the funds flow, not as claims.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clause 12 and confirm in writing that nothing is pre-agreed. **Reason:** The single default rule is how the 20% cap and 18-month limit migrate onto every other risk.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register (DD-012). Disclosure para 10 concedes that the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, along with share issue and transfer history, board minutes and any options or convertibles.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company. Check in particular whether Riverlark holds security over the shares.
  - At Completion: share certificates, signed transfer forms and releases of any encumbrances.
  - A fundamental title warranty at 100% of price (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Treat the register as a starting point and complete verification before signing. **Reason:** A company's own register is not proof of unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap and an 18-month limit.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax on the bonuses and any duty. It should be capped at 100% of price, run for 5–7 years, carry no basket, and give the Buyer conduct of claims.
  - **IP:** Ownership and non-infringement warranties at an elevated cap (for example 50–100%) with a longer limit of about 3–4 years. These should be linked to the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as OPEN and table Buyer drafts. **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed, and tax exposures routinely surface after the 18-month window.

## Other items to note
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Disclosure Letter avoids saying that consent *is not* required. It only says the documents do not describe consent as required. Have counsel confirm whether change-of-control or deemed-assignment provisions apply, and get the notification and consent letters delivered at Completion if needed.
- **Next step:** Return a full Buyer mark-up rather than an issues list limited to [OPEN] items. Ask the Seller to withdraw the "pre-cleared" characterisation.

- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are said to be ordinary-course costs. Disclosure para 8 asks that they be "read together" and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of DD-008 and DD-011 and an explanation of the timing. The renewals look as if they may have been split to stay under an approval threshold, and the Buyer should check for any related-party connection.
  - The renewals should be brought within the conduct-of-business covenants so that Buyer consent is required.
  - Any prepaid or committed amount not in the ordinary course should be treated as Debt, or covered by a specific indemnity.
  - The Buyer should get warranties that the renewals are on arm's-length terms and terminable.
- **Recommendation:** Hold as an open diligence item and add a price-adjustment hook. **Reason:** Three identical related renewals flagged to be read together is a red flag, not evidence of ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** The proposal that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" collapses all claim types into one regime. The [STANDARD] labelling also presents the package as agreed.
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct, expressly drafted regimes, each with its own cap, thresholds and time limit:
  1. General warranties
  2. Fundamental (title and capacity)
  3. Tax warranties and indemnity
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Sandbar)
  5. Fraud, which should be unlimited

  Price adjustments and Debt items should be dealt with in the funds flow, not as claims.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clause 12 and confirm in writing that nothing is pre-agreed. **Reason:** The single default rule is how the 20% cap and 18-month limit migrate onto every other risk.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register (DD-012). Disclosure para 10 concedes that the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, along with share issue and transfer history, board minutes and any options or convertibles.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company. Check in particular whether Riverlark holds security over the shares.
  - At Completion: share certificates, signed transfer forms and releases of any encumbrances.
  - A fundamental title warranty at 100% of price (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Treat the register as a starting point and complete verification before signing. **Reason:** A company's own register is not proof of unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap and an 18-month limit.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax on the bonuses and any duty. It should be capped at 100% of price, run for 5–7 years, carry no basket, and give the Buyer conduct of claims.
  - **IP:** Ownership and non-infringement warranties at an elevated cap (for example 50–100%) with a longer limit of about 3–4 years. These should be linked to the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as OPEN and table Buyer drafts. **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed, and tax exposures routinely surface after the 18-month window.

## Other items to note
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Disclosure Letter avoids saying that consent *is not* required. It only says the documents do not describe consent as required. Have counsel confirm whether change-of-control or deemed-assignment provisions apply, and get the notification and consent letters delivered at Completion if needed.
- **Next step:** Return a full Buyer mark-up rather than an issues list limited to [OPEN] items. Ask the Seller to withdraw the "pre-cleared" characterisation.
